title: NoSuchRemoteClusterException is returned for both non-existent remotes and remotes with skip_unavailable=true
body:
### Elasticsearch Version 8.14-SNAPSHOT ### Installed Plugins _No response_ ### Java Version _bundled_ ### OS Version Darwin michaels-mbp.lan 23.4.0 Darwin Kernel Version 23.4.0: Fri Mar 15 00:10:42 PDT 2024; root:xnu-10063.101.17~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000 arm64 ### Problem Description When doing cross-cluster searches (`_search` or `_async_search`), `NoSuchRemoteClusterException` is returned for both non-existent remotes and remotes with skip_unavailable=true that cannot be connected to. By contrast, remotes with skip_unavailable=false return a "connection_exception" error message when they cannot be reached. Should we also be returning "connection exception" errors for skip_unavailable=true remotes? Should NoSuchRemoteClusterException be reserved for attempts to search clusters that are not configured? This issue occurs for both non-secured and secured clusters. See the "Steps to Reproduce" section for details. ### Steps to Reproduce Manual testing. Configure a cluster to connect to two remote clusters. In my case, the three clusters all run on the same local machine and the config on the primary looks like: ``` cluster: remote: remote1: seeds: 127.0.0.1:9301 skip_unavailable: true remote2: seeds: 127.0.0.1:9302 skip_unavailable: false ```
#### Scenario 1: on a non-secured cluster, query for remote5 ``` POST remote5: */_async_search { ... query not shown ... } ``` You get a `NoSuchRemoteClusterException` (as expected)
Response example (toggle) ``` { "id": "FnFVcFctWTNxUnRDZlNzVVZFU2Q1dncaMWdWNHdULXdUaEtsUjc2UFJvTm9HZzoyNTk=", "is_partial": true, "is_running": false, "start_time_in_millis": 1712781379327, "expiration_time_in_millis": 1713213379327, "error": { "type": "status_exception", "reason": "error while executing search", "caused_by": { "type": "no_such_remote_cluster_exception", "reason": "no such remote cluster: [remote11]" } } } ```

#### Scenario 2: on a non-secured cluster, query for remote2 (skip_unavailable=false) when remote2 is not running/down You get a "not connected" type exception (as expected)
Response example (toggle) ``` { "id": "FnhXUkh5dTQ5U0ppdWlVNUFTeFF4MGcaMWdWNHdULXdUaEtsUjc2UFJvTm9HZzoxNTM=", "is_partial": true, "is_running": false, "start_time_in_millis": 1712781752071, "expiration_time_in_millis": 1713213752071, "error": { "type": "status_exception", "reason": "error while executing search", "caused_by": { "type": "connect_transport_exception", "reason": "[][127.0.0.1:9302] connect_exception", "caused_by": { "type": "uncategorized_execution_exception", "reason": "Failed execution", "caused_by": { "type": "execution_exception", "reason": "io.netty.channel.AbstractChannel$AnnotatedConnectException: Connection refused: /127.0.0.1:9302", "caused_by": { "type": "annotated_connect_exception", "reason": "Connection refused: /127.0.0.1:9302", "caused_by": { "type": "connect_exception", "reason": "Connection refused" } } } } } } } ```

#### Scenario 3: on a non-secured cluster, query for remote1 (skip_unavailable=true) when remote1 is not running/down In the search response you get a NoSuchRemoteClusterException: ``` // snippet of _cluster/details section in SearchResponse: "status": "skipped", "indices": "*", "timed_out": false, "failures": [ { "shard": -1, "index": null, "reason": { "type": "no_such_remote_cluster_exception", "reason": "no such remote cluster: [remote1]" } } ] ```

#### Secured clusters I believe the same issue occurs on a secured cluster. Example: in this test of [RemoteClusterSecurityFcActionAuthorizationIT](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/105792/files#diff-7e661242193b12735bd6cb53ce9be1edce2b8a74e5fa5b27039bdec8598e8f50R317), when the default value of skip_unavailable was changed from `false` to `true`, the search no longer throws the expected `ElasticsearchSecurityException`, but now instead throws `NoSuchRemoteClusterException`. ### Logs (if relevant) _No response_
